gloss: to change (footwear/legwear); to put on different shoes

definitions.explanation: To take off one pair of shoes, slippers, pants, or other items worn on the lower body and put on a different pair. Commonly used for changing shoes when entering a building.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}でスリッパに{履|は}き{替|か}えてください。
examples.english: Please change into slippers at the entrance.

examples.japanese: {運動靴|うんどうぐつ}に{履|は}き{替|か}えて{体育館|たいいくかん}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I changed into athletic shoes and went to the gym.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}タイヤに{履|は}き{替|か}える{時期|じき}だ。
examples.english: It's time to change to winter tires.

examples.japanese: {汚|よご}れたズボンを{履|は}き{替|か}えてから{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I changed out of my dirty pants before going out.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}に{着|つ}いたらまず{上履|うわば}きに{履|は}き{替|か}えなければならない。
examples.english: When you arrive at school, you have to change into indoor shoes first.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{履|は}き{替|か}える → {履|は}き{替|か}えない (negative)
・{履|は}き{替|か}える → {履|は}き{替|か}えて (te-form)
・{履|は}き{替|か}える → {履|は}き{替|か}えた (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {履|は}く (to wear on lower body/feet) + {替|か}える (to change/exchange)

USAGE:
Applies to anything worn on the lower body that is changed:
・{靴|くつ}を{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change shoes)
・スリッパに{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change into slippers)
・ズボンを{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change pants)
・タイヤを{履|は}き{替|か}える (to change tires - extended usage)

JAPANESE CULTURE:
Changing shoes is an important custom in Japan. At schools, workplaces, homes, and many public buildings, visitors change from outdoor shoes ({外履|そとば}き) to indoor shoes ({内履|うちば}き/{上履|うわば}き).

SIMILAR COMPOUND VERBS:
・{着替|きが}える - to change clothes (upper body/general)
・{乗|の}り{換|か}える - to transfer (vehicles)
